To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the risk of developing essential hypertension (EH), in adolescents with borderline hypertension is increased when the following characteristics are present: a family history of hypertension, a higher resting blood pressure and resting heart rate, a greater cardiovascular response during mental stress and a rhythmic cardiovascular re-sponse to mental stress, and (2) the presence of the aforementioned risk factors in adolescents with borderline blood pressure may be used to predict those who will develop fixed EH.
the cardiovascular characteristics of adolescents with borderline blood pressure are predictive of the development of essential (primary) hypertension.

The risk parameters for the devel opment of essential hypertension (E.H.) were evaluated in a group of adolescents who were normotensive, borderline hypertensive (systolic or diastolie blood pressure between the ninetieth and the ninety-fifth percentile) and who had a positive family history of E.H., compared to a normo ten sive, family history-negative control group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation and prediction of essential hypertension in adolescents.
the identification of the risk factors for the development of EH.
the identification of risk parameters for the early detection of EH in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of a strong family history, higher resting blood pressure, higher resting heart rates, and greater cardiovascular response to stress In adolescents with borderline hypertension are risk factors for the development of EH.
the presence of these risk parameters in adolescents with borderline hypertension may be a predictor of EH in this population.

the presence of a strong family history, higher blood pressures, higher heart rates, and a greater cardiovascular reactivity to stress, in addition to the presence of borderline hypertension, are risk factors for the development of EH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adolescents with borderline high blood pressure and a family history of essential hypertension have an increased risk of developing essential hypertension.
adolescents with borderline high blood pressure and certain characteristics have a higher chance of developing high blood pressure as adults.

adolescents with borderline blood pressure and a family history of hypertension are at increased risk for developing fixed hypertension, and this risk is further increased if these adolescents have an abnormal resting heart rate, an abnormal cardiovascular response to mental stimulation, or both.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a number of risk factors for developing hypertension in adolescents.
there are some adolescents that we can identify that are at high risk for developing high blood pressure as they get older.

adolescents with borderline elevated blood pressure should be followed closely and that those who have a strong family history, a high resting heart rate and blood pressure, and a large cardiovascular response to mental challenge should be monitored even more carefully.
